externalDestinations.title: Sell physical objects
externalDestinations.description: The sale of a tangible, material item in exchange for payment. The defining characteristic of this activity is the physical nature of the object being sold—an item that can be touched, weighed, and moved. This category applies to activities like selling products in a retail store, a used car through a private listing, or handmade crafts on an e-commerce platform. It is distinct from selling intangible items, such as services (e.g., consulting, repairs), digital goods (e.g., software, streaming media), or financial assets (e.g., stocks, bonds).

externalDestinations.title: Transform physical objects
externalDestinations.description: An activity that alters the intrinsic properties, state, or form of a physical object. As a type of 'Modify physical objects', this category focuses on changes *to* an object itself, distinguishing it from activities that change an object's location ('Move physical objects') or its relationship with other objects ('Assemble', 'Disassemble'). The scope is broad, encompassing transformations such as changing an object's physical or chemical state ('Heat', 'Develop (chemically)'), its shape ('Shape'), its surface ('Change surface', 'Clean'), or its operational condition ('Service', 'Adjust'). Examples include cleaning a window, shaping clay, heating a meal, servicing a machine, or painting a fence. Synonyms: Change, Transform, Work, Rework

externalDestinations.title: Inform
externalDestinations.description: The activity of making an actor aware of some fact, event, or state of affairs. Unlike the more general 'Send information', which may only cover the transmission of data, 'Inform' activities are characterized by the intent that the recipient receives and comprehends the information, resulting in new awareness or understanding. This is a broad category that includes many different methods of imparting knowledge, ranging in formality and purpose. For example, one can inform by 'Describing' details, 'Explaining' concepts, 'Announcing' news to a wide audience, issuing an 'Alert' about an urgent matter, casually 'Mentioning' a fact, or formally 'Testifying' in a legal setting. A primary way these activities are further categorized is by the subject of the informing action, such as another actor ('Inform Actor') or a piece of information ('Inform Information'). Synonyms: Advise, Inform

externalDestinations.title: Change surface
externalDestinations.description: A type of 'Transform physical objects' activity that alters the properties of an object's outermost layer—its surface—without changing its fundamental shape, structure, or assembly. These changes can affect appearance (such as color, pattern, or shininess), texture (such as smoothness or roughness), or protective qualities. This category includes activities that add a substance to the surface (e.g., 'Paint', 'Oil', 'Decorate'), modify the existing surface (e.g., 'Smooth', 'Polish', 'Refinish'), or create marks or indentations (e.g., 'Mark (physical)', 'Impress'). The key distinction is that the transformation is superficial; it does not alter the object's underlying form or assembly, which would be classified under activities like 'Change shape' or 'Assemble'. Synonyms: Change_surface

externalDestinations.title: Shape
externalDestinations.description: An activity that alters the physical form, structure, or configuration of an object. This type of transformation focuses on changing an object's geometric properties—its outline, surface, or internal arrangement—as distinct from changing its location, chemical composition, or state of matter (e.g., from solid to liquid). Shaping includes a wide variety of actions, from simple modifications like bending a wire, folding paper, or sharpening a blade, to more comprehensive processes like hammering metal or molding clay. This category covers both modifying an existing shape (e.g., 'Straighten' a bent rod) and creating a new shape from raw or pliable material (e.g., 'Form' a pot from clay). Synonyms: form, Change_shape, Shape

externalDestinations.title: Put physical objects
externalDestinations.description: The activity of placing a physical object or actor in a specific location or position. As a type of 'Move physical objects', this activity focuses on the final act of placement at a destination, distinguishing it from 'Take physical objects' (which focuses on the origin) and 'Carry physical objects' (which focuses on the transit between origin and destination). As a type of 'Put', it is concerned exclusively with tangible entities, in contrast to 'Put information'. This is a broad category that encompasses many specific methods of placement, which are reflected in its specializations. These methods include actions defined by their specific context or manner, such as 'Load' (placing into or onto a carrier), 'Raise' and 'Lower' (changing vertical position), 'Arrange' (placing in a specific order), 'Insert' (placing within another object), 'Install' (placing for operational use), and 'Hold' (maintaining a static position). The activity can also be specialized by what is being put, such as an inanimate object ('Position Physical Object') or an actor ('Position Actor'). Synonyms: Put

externalDestinations.title: Transform information
externalDestinations.description: An activity that changes the content, structure, format, or state of existing information. The core of this activity is taking existing information as input and producing a modified version as output. This distinguishes it from 'Create information', which brings new information into existence, and 'Analyze information', which seeks to understand information without altering it. The scope of transformation is broad, ranging from minor adjustments to substantial overhauls. It includes activities that alter the substance of the information, such as correcting, updating, or enhancing it ('Revise', 'Improve', 'Clean'); change its form or representation, such as reformatting its appearance ('Change Apperance') or converting it to a different system ('Encode'); or advance its state, such as moving it through a workflow ('Process'), preparing it for a specific use ('Prepare'), or bringing it to completion ('Finish'). Synonyms: Change, Transform, Work, Rework

externalDestinations.title: Select
externalDestinations.description: Choosing one or more options from a pre-existing set of alternatives. This focus on a pre-existing set distinguishes 'Select' from the more general 'Decide', which can also include generating new options before making a choice. The core of a 'Select' activity is the evaluation of and commitment to one or more items within a defined choice-space. The method of selection can vary widely, from systematic processes like analytical evaluation or applying explicit rules, to more subjective approaches like holistic intuition, social influence, negotiation, or even random chance. The object of selection is also a key dimension, and can be anything from information and events to actors (e.g., hiring a person). Importantly, this category also includes activities where the goal is not to choose an item itself, but to choose a label or make a judgment about it from a set of possible outcomes. Examples include 'Categorize' (choosing a folder for a file), 'Diagnose' (choosing an explanation for symptoms), and 'Validate' (choosing between 'valid' and 'invalid'). Synonyms: Choose

externalDestinations.title: Send information
externalDestinations.description: The activity of transmitting information from a sender to one or more recipients. As a type of 'Provide information', this category focuses on the active transmission of information, distinguishing it from more passive ways of making it available, such as simply storing it where others might find it. This is a very broad category that encompasses any act of communication where information is conveyed from one party to another. The specific types of 'Send information' activities can be distinguished by many factors, including: - The communicative intent: such as to 'Inform' someone of a fact, 'Request' an action, 'Advise' on a decision, 'Propose' an idea, or make a 'Promise'. - The medium or modality: such as through spoken language ('Talk'), visual display ('Show'), or digital transfer ('Upload'). - The social context or role in a conversation: such as to 'Greet' someone, 'Answer' a question, or 'Relay' a message from another source. Synonyms: Send, Transmit

externalDestinations.title: Control
externalDestinations.description: Activities that involve exercising direct influence, power, or authority to determine or regulate the state, behavior, or outcome of something. As a form of 'Lead', control is characterized by its direct and often binding nature, as opposed to more indirect forms of guidance or persuasion. This category encompasses a wide range of actions, from hands-on manipulation (e.g., 'Operate' a machine, 'Steer' a vehicle) to the exercise of formal authority (e.g., 'Authorize' a transaction, 'Manage' a team, 'Order' a subordinate). The nature of control can be proactive ('Start', 'Organize'), reactive ('Punish'), permissive ('Authorize'), restrictive ('Prevent'), or involve ongoing oversight ('Manage'). The object of control can be tangible or abstract, including information, physical objects, events, or other actors. Synonyms: Synonyms: Control

externalDestinations.title: Create Image
externalDestinations.description: Synonyms: Develop Image, Generate Image, Make Image, Produce Image

externalDestinations.title: Separate physical objects
externalDestinations.description: An activity that modifies physical objects by dividing a single entity into multiple parts or by detaching connected entities. As a type of 'Modify physical objects', the defining outcome is an increase in the number of distinct physical objects or a reduction in their physical connections. This is the conceptual opposite of 'Combine physical objects'. This category covers a wide range of methods. These can be forceful actions that alter an object's integrity, such as 'Cut' with a sharp tool or 'Break' through impact. They can also be methodical processes that undo existing connections, such as 'Disassemble' equipment, 'Disconnect' cables, 'Unpack' items from a container, or 'Remove' one object from another. Synonyms: Separate, Divide

externalDestinations.title: Adjust (information)
externalDestinations.description: Activities that involve making modifications to existing information to bring it into a more desirable or effective state, such as to correct it, improve its fit for a purpose, or align it with a standard. This type of transformation is distinct from creating a new representation of the information (e.g., summarizing, translating). Instead, it focuses on incremental changes to the original. Common types of adjustment include altering, adapting, aligning, customizing, or regulating information to meet specific requirements. Synonyms: Adjust

externalDestinations.title: Cover
externalDestinations.description: An activity that involves placing one object over, on, or around another, typically to protect, conceal, decorate, or contain it. As a type of 'Combine physical objects', covering is distinct from activities like 'Attach' or 'Assemble' because it does not necessarily create a permanent or structural bond. For example, putting a lid on a jar is an act of covering, while welding two metal plates together is not. The specific manner of covering can vary, such as by completely enclosing something ('Envelop'), placing an item on a surface ('Put On'), or distributing a substance across an area ('Spread'). The entity being covered can be an inanimate object or an actor, such as a person. Synonyms: Synonyms: Cover
